$comment: Space-programme library. Every engineering coefficient the fixture generator and the
engine need lives here rather than as a literal in code, so a site can be re-calibrated
by editing data instead of recompiling. Each entry carries the source it came from.
Heat-balance contract, so nothing is counted twice:
baseHeatLoad  = lightingWPerM2 x area  +  fixedEquipmentW   (always-present gain)
solar         = solarGainMultiplier x solarPeakWPerM2 x area
Equipment power density is deliberately absent from the programmes: it is plugs.go's
job. Putting it in both places is how a cooling load gets double-counted.

calibration.source: Hoang et al. 2021, 57 commercial+government offices, doi:10.55066/proc-icec.2021.19

endUseShares.source: Luong et al. 2025, 45-storey Hanoi tower, doi:10.54772/jomc.v15i02.1190

calibration.gridEmissionFactorSource: Vietnam national grid factor 2022, quoted in Luong et al. 2025

furnishingCapacitanceNote: Room air alone gives a time constant of minutes; real rooms respond over hours
because furniture, partitions and slab surface couple to the air. A lumped 4-6x
multiplier on air capacitance is the standard single-node way to represent that,
and it is what puts identified time constants in the 2-10 h band an office shows.
This is the one number here that is a modelling choice rather than a measurement;
once a room is identified from real data its measured time constant supersedes it.
physics.occupantSensibleSource: ASHRAE Fundamentals, seated light office work, sensible portion
physics.outdoorAirSource: QCVN 09:2017/BXD and ASHRAE 62.1 office ventilation rate
ventilationEnthalpyNote: Total (sensible + latent) enthalpy drop from Ho Chi Minh design outdoor air
(33 C, ~75% RH, ~88 kJ/kg) to the AHU supply condition (~12 C saturated,
~33 kJ/kg). In a tropical climate this fresh-air load is the LARGEST single
cooling term and is mostly latent -- dehumidifying the outdoor air, not cooling
it. Omitting it is why a twin calibrated only on internal gains under-reports a
Vietnamese office by roughly a third. Recomputed live against the weather feed
when outdoor humidity is available; this is the design-day fallback.
solarGainReferenceNote: Solar gain for a zone whose aperture multiplier is 1.0. This records, rather than
fixes, a KNOWN DIVERGENCE: the heat-balance contract at the top of this file says
solar = solarGainMultiplier x solarPeakWPerM2 x area, but engine.go has always
evaluated solarGainMultiplier x 10000 W with no area term at all -- equivalent to
assuming every zone is 1000 m2, where the fixture's median zone is 12.6 m2. The
literal was moved here so it is visible and site-editable; it was NOT re-scaled,
because doing so drops building-wide solar from 259.5 kW to 9.1 kW and that is a
recalibration decision, not a refactor. Only 45 of 735 zones have any aperture.
Correct fix: scale by exteriorWallM2 x glazing fraction and recalibrate this figure
as a facade irradiance, then delete this key.
physics.daylightReferenceNote: Indoor illuminance corresponding to solarGainReferenceW, so a BH1750 reading divided by this is a pure scaling ratio on that zone's solar term (simulation/engine.go solarGainW). Used only while the zone's lights are OFF -- an indoor lux sensor under lit luminaires is measuring electric lighting, whose heat is already in baseHeatLoad.
physics.designCopNote: Plant COP at nominal lift; simulation/engine.go degrades from this as the building is strained. Superseded, for the portion of the building on a real AC clamp, by the COP measured as thermal delivered over electrical drawn.
physics.copCurveNote: How far COP falls per degC of average zone strain, and the bounds on the resulting curve. Previously literals in engine.go broadcast().
physics.eflhNote: Office EFLH for a Vietnamese commercial building on a ~11 h day, 5.5 d week, year-round cooling. Converts a design-day peak to an annual intensity for the cohort check.
physics.supplyAirNote: Design AHU discharge. Superseded per zone by a measured supply-air probe when one reports (edge/esp32 SUPPLY_C).
physics.supplyAirDesignAchNote: Design supply-air rate for comfort cooling, in air changes per hour of the zone's own volume. It is what sizes each VAV: the network solver needs a per-box design flow, and without one it split a FIXED fan capacity evenly across however many boxes the building happened to have — 21.9 m3/s through each of a house's two VAVs, ~150,000 m3/h for 72 m2. 4-8 ACH is the usual band for sensible cooling; raise it for high-gain spaces once the plant has been balanced.
physics.ahuDesignPressureNote: Design AHU static pressure the VAV resistances are referenced to, and the operating point the fan curve is scaled to hit for THIS building.
physics.hvacLoadPerDegCNote: Fractional change in cooling ELECTRICAL draw per degC of setpoint or deadband relaxation. The widely-replicated commercial-HVAC rule of thumb is 3-5%/degC; 5% is the upper end and is used both to price overcooling and to size what a pre-cool window can coast off the evening peak. Recalibrate per site once the plant has been metered across a setpoint change.
physics.precoolShiftNote: Fraction of the plant's current cooling ELECTRICAL draw a thermal-mass pre-charge can shift out of the EVN cao diem window. Same order as hvacLoadPerDegCFraction because a pre-cool window is in effect a ~1 degC setpoint depression held ahead of the peak. This is an estimate until the building has been measured coasting; the UI must label it as one.
physics.outdoorCo2Note: Ambient outdoor CO2. The floor every indoor concentration is measured from; an urban Vietnamese site runs a little above the global background, so recalibrate from a sensor left outdoors rather than assuming the textbook 420.
physics.co2PpmPerOccupantNote: Steady-state CO2 rise per occupant in a zone ventilated at outdoorAirLPerSPerPerson. Used ONLY to display a modelled concentration where no NDIR sensor reports, and every surface that shows it must label it as modelled — a fabricated ppm on a channel that implies measurement is exactly what rule 1 forbids.
nonHvacBaseNote: Lighting + fans + lifts + pumps as a floor-area-scaled baseline, replacing a fixed
1.15 MW that was sized for the mis-digitized data-centre fixture and did not move
when the building did. Derived from the case-study shares: outdoor lighting 16.1%
+ ventilation 15.3% + indoor lighting 9.1% + lifts 7.8% + pumps 0.2% = 48.5% of a
109.6 kWh/m2.yr cohort EUI, over ~3000 equivalent full-load hours.
physics.minZoneCapacitanceNote: Numerical floor for the explicit-Euler integration only. The raw digitizer fixture carried 39 kJ/K rooms with 85 kW in them, which ran away; with capacitance derived from real volume this floor should never bind. Raise it if a small zone oscillates.
physics.uValueWallNote: Vietnamese commercial facade: single or lightly-coated glazing over concrete, no continuous insulation. QCVN 09:2017/BXD sets the envelope OTTV ceiling; 2.8 is a representative assembly U for existing stock rather than new-build best practice.
physics.uValueRoofNote: Exposed roof slab on the top floor only.
physics.rInNote: Split of total envelope resistance into inside-surface (air film + inner mass) and outside-surface halves for the 2R1C. Replaces a hardcoded 'rWall/2 and rWall/2 + 0.1' in engine.go, where that fixed +0.1 K/W swamped any realistic envelope: a real facade is ~0.005 K/W total.
uValuePartitionNote: EFFECTIVE coupling through internal partitions, W/m2K of partition area -- not the
partition's own U-value, which is nearer 2.0 for uninsulated plasterboard or light
block. The reduction is deliberate: the 2R1C has a single outdoor node, so partition
conductance to a NEIGHBOUR that sits at nearly the same temperature has to be entered
as a smaller coupling to outdoors, or a core zone is modelled as though the room next
door were the weather. Roughly 0.4 of the assembly U, i.e. the fraction of the outdoor
temperature difference that actually appears across the partition.
This is a calibration choice, like furnishingCapacitanceMultiplier, and is stated as
one: it is set so identified time constants land in the 2-10 h band real offices show.
A room identified from its own measured data supersedes it.
Applied to partition area, not floor area -- floor-area coupling cancels against a
floor-area capacitance and hands every core zone an identical time constant.

planning.$comment: Area bands a space planner uses, m2. Drives programme assignment from geometry.
planning.sliverNote: Below this a polygon is a segmentation artifact (wall cavity, column enclosure, duct shaft), not a room. Not conditioned, not credited, not identified.
planning.facadeDepthNote: A zone whose centroid is within one room-depth of the exterior wall sees solar; core zones do not.
planning.facadeToleranceNote: A polygon edge whose midpoint lies within this distance of the building's exterior outline is counted as external wall.

occupancy.$comment: How many people the engine puts in a room. Design occupancy is the zone's own digitized floor area over its programme's areaPerOccupantM2; the diurnal profile below says what fraction of that is present each hour. Both are building coefficients, so both live here.

profileNotes.$comment: Fraction of a zone's DESIGN occupancy (floor area / areaPerOccupantM2) present in each hour, index 0..23 local time. The engine multiplies the two to get a zone's occupancy; a zone bound to a real occupancy sensor ignores these entirely and uses the measurement.
profileNotes.officeSource: ASHRAE 90.1-2019 Appendix G, Table G-D, weekday occupancy fraction for office occupancies.
profileNotes.meetingNote: A meeting room is at its design density only while a meeting is running; the daily mean is far below it.
profileNotes.lobbyNote: Peaks at the two commute shoulders rather than mid-morning.
profileNotes.residentialLivingNote: HCMC tube house: the household leaves for work and school through the morning and the living space fills again after 17:00. Estimated for this dwelling type from the site survey, not measured - a prior for the identification to supersede.
profileNotes.homeOfficeNote: A study in a house: worked during the day and again after dinner.
profileNotes.bedroomNote: Inverse of every other profile - occupied overnight.
profileNotes.transientNote: Programmes with no areaPerOccupantM2: a bathroom, passage, corridor, store, plant room or comms room has no standing population. People pass through, but a design occupancy for them does not exist and inventing one puts a ventilation load on the plant that nobody is there to need. A PIR or CV node bound to such a zone overrides this.

occupancy.jitterNote: Household and desk counts are not identical from one day to the next. A deterministic schedule makes every learned baseline's spread collapse to zero, so the first real variation scores as an unbounded anomaly. This is the standard deviation of the hour-to-hour draw, as a fraction of the scheduled count.
occupancy.resampleNote: How often the scheduled count is redrawn. Long enough that a room is not flickering between counts, short enough that the identification sees occupancy move within an hour.

storage.$comment: Battery energy storage, when the site has not declared a real one. A BESS is an ASSET, not a physical coefficient: a deployment that owns a pack sets BESS_POWER_MW and BESS_CAPACITY_MWH to its nameplate and none of this is read. These figures only size the modelled pack that the twin shows when nobody has said what is installed, and they are expressed relative to the building so the same defaults are sane at both ends of the range this engine runs at.
storage.powerNote: Inverter rating as a fraction of the building's own observed peak load. Commercial peak-shaving packs are sized to shave the top of the curve, not to carry the whole building. The previous default was a flat 2 MW / 4 MWh — sized for a ~17 MW campus and left unchanged when the engine was pointed at a 72 m2 house, where it was 80x the entire building load and covered 100% of it, so grid draw read zero all through the evening peak.
storage.hoursNote: Usable energy as hours at the inverter rating. Two hours is the standard commercial duration and covers EVN's 5-hour evening peak window at partial depth.
storage.minPowerNote: Below this the modelled pack is not worth showing and the BESS is reported as absent, rather than drawn as a battery that shaves single watts.

open-office.lightingSource: QCVN 09:2017/BXD and ASHRAE 90.1 LED office LPD

comms-room.note: One per floor. A floor comms room is a rack or two on a small split unit. Critical: never swept, never set back.

plant-room.note: AHU / riser plant. Ventilated, not comfort-conditioned. Critical: never swept, never set back.

kitchen.lightingSource: Residential LED tube/strip as observed on site — roughly half the 9 W/m2 office LPD
kitchen.note: Vietnamese tube-house rear service space. fixedEquipmentW is the always-on residential base (fridge duty-cycle average + RO purifier standby). Cooking is bottled gas here and adds NO electrical load.

living.note: Setpoint deliberately above the 24 C office figure: HCMC residential comfort expectations sit higher and the AC runs intermittently rather than being held all day.

bedroom.note: Not in the current ground-floor scan; defined now so an upper-floor scan needs no library change.

home-office.note: A study in a house, not a commercial office: fewer occupants, lower LPD, higher setpoint. fixedEquipmentW covers the VNPT router and a desk machine idling.

bathroom.note: Unconditioned wet room. High setpoint + wide deadband keep the optimizer from ever trying to cool it.

circulation.note: Passage / stair core — residential equivalent of `corridor`, unconditioned.

$residentialNote: Residential programmes added 2026-07-26 for the HCMC tube-house deployment scanned with
Polycam (tools/housify_fixture.py). The office programmes above describe a commercial
tower and do NOT transfer to a house: lighting densities are roughly half, setpoints sit
2-4 C higher, and cooking contributes no electrical load because it is bottled gas.
These densities are ENGINEERING ESTIMATES for this dwelling type, not measured values and
not code minima. They are priors for the RLS identification to supersede (rule 4), and
they are the first numbers to replace once the PZEM is actually metering the house.
